findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: The Meet-to-Cal-Video fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null check. If the array is missing or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and this throws before any calendar or video event is created. Bookings that use Google Meet and have no destination calendar (previously safe via optional chaining) will 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Organizer attendee email is always the first host calendar
findings.body: createEvent and updateEvent pick `destinationCalendar[0]` and, when that entry has an externalId, send it as the organizer attendee's email on every insert/update. EventManager now calls this once per host credential and passes the full array, while the calendarId is chosen by credentialId. Secondary hosts therefore get an event on their own calendar whose organizer email is the first host's calendar id. Google treats that field as an attendee email, so the insert can be rejected as an invalid attendee or the event is attributed to the wrong person. The organizer email must be the destination that matches this credential, or the organizer's real email.

findings.title: Update/delete no longer fall back to a destination calendar
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. That comparison is against a falsy id, so it never matches, and the Google call is made with `calendarId: undefined` (delete then substitutes "primary"). Previously these methods used `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Reschedules, location edits, and cancellations that lack a stored externalCalendarId will hit the wrong calendar or fail, leaving the original event in place.

findings.title: Outlook creates every host event on the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent still ignores the credentialId CalendarManager now passes and always builds the Graph URL from `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. For a collective booking EventManager invokes createEvent once per host credential with that host's token but the shared array. A second Outlook host therefore writes into the first host's calendar id (usually 404) or, if the first entry has no externalId, into the caller's default calendar rather than their configured destination. The same first-element-only pattern is in Lark (`CalendarService.ts` create/update/delete) and CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` createEvent filter), so non-Google hosts still do not get their own events.

findings.title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: Host destination calendars are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. The field is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so optional chaining skips the push. Collective co-hosts who do have a calendar connected then never get an event created, which is the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize to an array before pushing team calendars.

findings.title: Cancelling all recurring instances drops extra host calendars
findings.body: The new loop walks every calendar reference, but the recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch ignores that reference and, for each updated booking, does `references.find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. Only the first calendar reference is deleted, and the block runs once per outer reference using every calendar credential, so the first event is deleted repeatedly while other hosts' recurring events are never removed. Non-recurring cancel uses each reference's uid and credential; recurring cancel must do the same per updated booking reference.

findings.title: Missing credential fails the entire calendar update silently
findings.body: After the DB lookup, `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still pushed when `credential` is undefined (deleted or no app slug). `getCalendar(undefined)` throws, the catch abandons every reference in the batch, and the previous `console.error(message)` was removed, so reschedule and location updates fail with no log. Skip a missing credential (or record that one failure) instead of failing the whole update, and keep the error log.

findings.title: Organization slug condition was inverted
findings.body: Unrelated to destination calendars, the create payload changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. When team billing is off, new organizations are stored with no slug. When it is on, slug is written immediately as well as `requestedSlug`, which skips the previous "slug only after billing" behavior. This will break org URLs or billing gating and should not be in this PR.
